title: Supreme Court tells Bengal voter-roll tribunals to hear deleted voters first, Kolkata on priority
dek: Appeals against added names are deferred and the Election Commission must add tribunals. Hearing the state's ward-map appeal, judges asked how a dissolved corporation could recommend new wards.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Supreme Court on Monday told the tribunals hearing West Bengal's voter-roll appeals to put people struck off the rolls first, and to take up appeals from the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) area ahead of others because the city's civic elections are due. It also directed the Election Commission of India (ECI) to add tribunals, in consultation with the Calcutta High Court, and to find more premises across Kolkata so that appellants can reach them.

A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana passed the interim directions in Mostari Banu v. Election Commission of India, one of the petitions challenging the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), the Commission's door-to-door re-verification of voters. Appeals from people who say they were wrongly removed are to be heard before appeals against names that were added. "The second set of appeals does not involve any urgency, and those appeals may, for the time being, be deferred," the bench said, according to reports of the order. "The first set of appeals shall be given preference in the matter of final disposal."

## What the court heard

Prashant Bhushan, for the petitioners, said that of about 38 lakh appeals filed, just over one lakh had been decided, and that most of those had gone in favour of the deleted voters. Reports differ on his figure: some put the share at 93 per cent, another at 98 per cent. He said about 22 lakh appeals seeking restoration to the rolls were pending, and that more than two lakh voters from the Kolkata municipal area had been excluded and were still waiting, reports said. Some 16 lakh appeals challenging inclusions are also pending, according to reports. The court did not verify these figures.

Gopal Sankaranarayanan, also for the petitioners, said the ECI's own affidavit showed that the state's Chief Electoral Officer had filed appeals against inclusions, and argued that the officer had no power to do so. Because such appeals go to an officer the Commission designates, he said, it was "effectively an appeal from the Election Commission to itself", according to reports.

Petitioners also raised a state Food Department notification that links verification of ration-card beneficiaries to the SIR's results. Justice Bagchi said the concern was not a "bald assertion" given the notification, but that the court was making no finding that anyone had lost benefits, reports said; the bench said people affected could go to the High Court. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta asked why such people were not approaching the High Courts and said the forum was being used for publicity, according to reports.

## The Kolkata election knot

Kolkata has had no elected council since June, when Mayor Firhad Hakim of the Trinamool Congress resigned, the state dissolved the corporation and an administrator was appointed. The state government then raised the number of wards from 144 to 209. On 6 November a Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court barred the State Election Commission from calling the KMC election on the new ward map until a single judge decides the challenge to it.

The state government has asked the Supreme Court to set that order aside (State of West Bengal v. Dipu Das, SLP(C) 40151-40152/2026). When the same bench heard it on Monday afternoon, its judges questioned how the new wards had been drawn. The KMC Act allows its schedule of wards to be amended either at the state's discretion or on the corporation's recommendation, and Justice Bagchi asked about a 3 July communication that sought a recommendation from the dissolved corporation. "If you are getting a recommendation from a corporation which does not exist, how will you exercise power?" he asked, according to reports, adding that the central question was "who is acting under whose directions" and that it was "more a question of Caesar's wife", a reference to the principle that the process must be above suspicion.

The bench also said the state was not barred from increasing the number of wards while the corporation was dissolved, reports said. Solicitor General Mehta argued that the state, not the civic body, had carried out the exercise: the Urban Development Department invited objections and appointed 10 officers to hear them, and during a dissolution the municipal commissioner acts on the state's directions. He said the increase in wards itself had not been challenged in the High Court, only the way the boundaries were drawn. The court passed no order on the appeal. The petitioners in the High Court argue that an administrator could not stand in for the elected corporation in recommending the new wards, and allege the boundaries were drawn to help one party. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has said Kolkata, Howrah and Siliguri will vote in February.

The roll problem is separate but linked. Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer postponed the annual Special Summary Revision of the rolls, which was due to start on Monday, citing "unavoidable circumstances", with reports pointing to the tribunal backlog. The ECI set up 19 appellate tribunals in March, according to reports. On 21 November the Trinamool Congress, the CPI(M) and the Congress held a joint convention in Kolkata and asked the State Election Commission to hold the Kolkata and Howrah polls only after the revision ends in January. Reports put pending appeals from those two cities at between 1.6 lakh and 1.7 lakh.

## What happens next

The ECI must now consult the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court on how many tribunals to add and where in Kolkata to put them. The written order on the tribunals had not been posted on the Supreme Court's website at the time of writing. The state's appeal on the ward map is due to be heard again on Wednesday, 25 November, one report said; another gave no date. Until it is decided, the High Court's bar stands and the KMC election cannot be notified. The administrator's term at the corporation ends on 7 December, according to reports.
